title: a-proof-that-binds-an-added-name-at-import-is-red-at-proveme-not-unran-at-hollow
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; codemother owns the care of the code (memory codemonkey-owns-builder-processes — inspectors and gates are its things); cairn/tools/proof_coverage is a tool with users (the PROVEME crossing, the tester).
questions: none, because his 'yes ticket' (CairnCommons/ideas/2026-09-14-yes-ticket-as-to-the-loop-residue.json) answers the only spec question (does the pattern earn a ticket); the instrument's seat and shape are settled by measurement of the three instances (commits a38204e, e1dcc6e; proof_coverage.py's in-line note of 2026-09-10) and recorded in assumption_check.
intention: A proof that binds a name its build added at import time is red at PROVEME, by name and line, before the hollow reading spends its budget to say UNRAN.
why: Law 8 (a proof a hollow build could not pass — a proof that crashes before its first tooth when its subject is removed proves nothing about that subject, and hollow already refuses to count it either way; this moves the refusal to where the proof is written, which is where it is cheap); Law 4 (three measured instances — 2026-09-10 crossings.py, 2026-09-13 a38204e artifact door, 2026-09-14 e1dcc6e test_exemption_set.py — each fixed by hand after a 2–5 minute hollow run and a paragraph in hollow's own output; the rule is prose that has now chafed three times, so it becomes a sieve); Law 1 (the third session re-derived the same fix from the same message; a sieve settles it).
how: One sieve in cairn/tools/proof_coverage (the PROVEME instrument that already reads a ticket's PROVES-carrying proofs): `proof_binds_its_subject_at_call_time`. For each proof named in the ticket's coverage, walk its MODULE-LEVEL imports with ast, transitively through cairn-rooted modules (bounded depth, module-level statements only), and resolve each imported name to a file and a definition. Compare against what the build ADDED: files absent at the pre-build commit (the BUILDME crossing's commit, via git diff --diff-filter=A) and top-level names absent in the pre-build version of a file that existed. Any module-level binding of an added file or added name is a lack, naming the proof, the line, the import, and the fix in the words hollow already prints ('resolve the names this build ADDED at call time'). Red at PROVEME; the hollow reading is then reached only by proofs that can survive their subject being taken away. Plus the guidance line where a proof is written: /sail's step 3 ('Prove — twice') gains one sentence naming the rule and the sieve; the tester's charter names the sieve as hollow's front door.
falsifier: DONE when: (1) a fixture proof doing `from <added_module> import x` at module level, beside a fixture ticket whose pre-build commit lacks that module, is red under proof_binds_its_subject_at_call_time naming the proof, line and name; the same import moved inside main() is green; (2) the transitive case (proof imports A at module level; A imports an added name from B at module level) is red naming the chain; (3) the three historical instances rebuilt as fixtures each red at the line the hand fix touched; (4) a fixture ticket at PROVEME with the red proof does not reach the hollow reading (the sieve reds first) — and with the sieve reverted the same fixture reads UNRAN under hollow (the self-reference tooth); (5) /sail's SKILL.md step 3 carries the sentence and skills/sail's proof reads it. Horizon: one build. WRONG INTENT if the walk reads green over a proof hollow then reads UNRAN on a live ticket — then the instrument moves into hollow as a pre-flight import of each proof against the reverted world, and the static walk retires.
traces_to: Law 8 (a proof a hollow build could not pass — a proof that crashes before its first tooth when its subject is removed proves nothing about that subject, and hollow already refuses to count it either way; this moves the refusal to where the proof is written, which is where it is cheap); Law 4 (three measured instances — 2026-09-10 crossings.py, 2026-09-13 a38204e artifact door, 2026-09-14 e1dcc6e test_exemption_set.py — each fixed by hand after a 2–5 minute hollow run and a paragraph in hollow's own output; the rule is prose that has now chafed three times, so it becomes a sieve); Law 1 (the third session re-derived the same fix from the same message; a sieve settles it).

watchme.trigger: every hollow reading (bin/cairn test --hollow) — the tester pokes the probe after the run with the count of UNRAN files; and every proof_coverage run at PROVEME with the count of proof_binds_its_subject_at_call_time lacks. No poller.
watchme.enough: 20 hollow readings after the build with ZERO UNRAN files attributed to a module-level import (hollow's `broke` set) — or ONE UNRAN that the sieve read green on the same ticket, which is the finding and the WRONG-INTENT clause (the static walk missed a binding; the instrument moves into hollow).
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier: hollow readings counted, UNRAN files by cause, sieve lacks counted, and every UNRAN the sieve did not predict with its import chain.
watchme.nexus: the proof-quality tree — the same readings proof_coverage and hollow already feed; this probe is the first that measures the two instruments AGAINST each other.
watchme.consumer: Akien, and codemother (owner of the care of the code) when it reviews proofs.

gates_bound: code-seam gate-set: BUILDME rides the intent berth and the sorted berth (buildme_rides_the_intent, buildme_rides_the_sorted) and the_ticket_has_every_answer_it_needs (none opened). PROVEME: proofs sealed green with current fingerprint; hollow reading over every writes_to file — and this ticket's own proofs must bind proof_coverage at call time, or the sieve it builds reds the ticket that built it (the self-reference tooth, same shape as 9adc6fddf185's); proof_coverage naming a tooth per falsifier clause. PROVED: verdict artifact against the falsifier. Feeds back to origin on failure.
children: none, because the seam is one sieve in one existing tool plus one sentence and one charter edge, all in one build; the fallback (a pre-flight inside hollow) is the falsifier's WRONG-INTENT route, not a child.
depends_on: d2ecdb867bc9 (crossings record — the pre-build commit the sieve diffs against); the tester's hollow reading (cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py) as the backstop and the WATCHME's other instrument.
